title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In this continuation of the Longue Marche, Grothendieck builds a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group, written Π~ or Γ~ (the symbol is ambiguous in the image), from the 'équation des lacets'. It is meant to contain the Galois group Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q).

Notation, as far as it can be read:
- \hat π_{0,3} is the profinite free group on two generators, the geometric fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}.
- Ĉ^+_{0,3} ≅ PSL(2,Z)^ ≅ \hat π_{0,3} ⋊ S_3. Here Γ(2)/±1 is free of rank 2 and normal in PSL(2,Z), with quotient S_3 = PSL(2,Z/2). This is the geometric '+' (orientation-preserving) modular group in genus 0.
- M~_{0,3} is the extension 1 → Ĉ^+_{0,3} → M~_{0,3} → Π~ → 1. It contains the arithmetic group M_{0,3}, which lies over Γ_Q ⊂ Π~.

Previous page. He constructed a homomorphism φ' : M~_{0,3} → GL(2,\hat Z)' = GL(2,\hat Z)/±1 lying over a character χ : Π~ → \hat Z^×. He then pulled back the central extension 1 → ±1 → GL(2,\hat Z) → GL(2,\hat Z)' → 1 along φ'. This gives a central extension Ñ_{1,1} of M~_{0,3} by ±1, with a lift φ : Ñ_{1,1} → GL(2,\hat Z) (diagram 19).

This page.

(i) Comparison with the classical map. On the arithmetic subgroup M_{0,3}, φ' should agree with the classical 'modular' homomorphism of §39 (1). That classical map is the Galois/monodromy representation on the Tate module of the universal elliptic curve, via the Legendre family, modulo ±1. It suffices to check this on the decomposition-type subgroups Γ_{Q,σ} ⊂ Π~ lying over Γ_Q. He says this should be easy and admits it without proof.

(ii) Identifications. Granting (i), the preimage of M_{0,3} in Ñ_{1,1} is N_{1,1}, the arithmetic fundamental group of the moduli stack M_{1,1} over Q. Its geometric part is the preimage of Ĉ^+_{0,3} ≅ PSL(2,Z)^, namely Ĉ^+_{1,1} ≅ SL(2,Z)^ = π_1(M_{1,1,Q̄}). This is the profinite incarnation of SL(2,Z) → PSL(2,Z) with kernel ±1, i.e. M_{1,1} as a ±1-gerbe over the S_3-quotient of the λ-line.

(iii) Diagram (20). There is a morphism of extensions
1 → SL(2,Z)^ → Ñ_{1,1} → Π~ → 1
mapping to
1 → SL(2,\hat Z) → GL(2,\hat Z) → \hat Z^× → 1 (the last map being det).
The left vertical arrow is the congruence map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,\hat Z), the middle is φ, and the right is χ. Over Γ_Q this recovers the classical diagram: π_1(M_{1,1,Q}) → GL_2(\hat Z), the Tate-module representation of the universal elliptic curve, with det equal to the cyclotomic character.

Purpose. The next page says he has thereby reconstructed, purely from Aut(\hat π_{0,3}), the 'arithmetic' diagram of §39, enlarged from Γ_Q to the GT-like group Π~. What remains is to characterize Γ_Q inside Π~, and to ask what becomes of the splitting (3).
errors: Gap, explicitly admitted: the agreement of φ' with the classical modular homomorphism on M_{0,3} (via the subgroups Γ_{Q,σ}) is not proved.

The claim that the preimage of M_{0,3} is N_{1,1} is hedged by Grothendieck himself ('à isom. près', 'en tous cas' only the geometric part). It relies on (i) and on identifying the pulled-back ±1 extension with SL(2,Z)^ → PSL(2,Z)^. The latter is correct: the pullback of SL(2,\hat Z) → PSL(2,\hat Z) along PSL(2,Z)^ → PSL(2,\hat Z) is SL(2,Z)^, since −1 survives in completions. This is plausible but not argued on the page.

The left vertical arrow SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,\hat Z) is surjective but not injective (failure of the congruence subgroup property). The diagram is fine as stated, but φ is not injective on the geometric part.

ideas.what: Pulling back the central extension GL_2(\hat Z) → GL_2(\hat Z)/±1 along a homomorphism defined on the extended (GT-type) automorphism group of \hat π_{0,3}. This yields a genus-one group Ñ_{1,1} lying over the GT-like group Π~.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of GT actions from genus 0 to M_{1,1}; GT acting on SL(2,Z)^ (genus-one GT)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (GT with genus-one relation, 1997); Nakamura–Schneps (subgroup of GT acting on the profinite genus-one mapping class group, ~2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'Teichmüller tower' and genus one, but not this explicit diagram

ideas.what: Identification of PSL(2,Z)^ with \hat F_2 ⋊ S_3 (the geometric + group Ĉ^+_{0,3}), and of its ±1 central extension with SL(2,Z)^ = π_1(M_{1,1,Q̄})

Diagram (20): a morphism of extensions from (SL(2,Z)^ → Ñ_{1,1} → Π~) to (SL(2,\hat Z) → GL(2,\hat Z) → \hat Z^×), with χ the cyclotomic-type character on Π~. This extends the Tate-module representation of the universal elliptic curve from Gal(Q̄/Q) to the GT-like group.
ideas.modern_name: GT-extension of the l-adic/adelic Galois representation of the universal elliptic curve; λ-character of GT
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Galois representation via Legendre family, 1980s); Nakamura; Hain–Matsumoto (relative completion of SL_2(Z) with GT/Galois actions)

missed.claim: Grothendieck asserts, without proof, that the homomorphism φ' : M~_{0,3} → GL_2(\hat Z)/±1, built purely group-theoretically from Aut(\hat π_{0,3}), agrees on the arithmetic subgroup with the classical modular (Legendre / Tate-module) representation. He reduces this to a check on the subgroups Γ_{Q,σ}.
missed.quote: Il faudrait vérifier que l'hom φ' qu'on vient de construire coïncide sur M_{0,3} ⊂ M~_{0,3} avec l'hom. "modulaire" bien connu ... je vais l'admettre ici.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a purely combinatorial (GT-side) construction of a GL_2(\hat Z)-valued representation of a GT-type group, compatible with the Galois representation of the universal elliptic curve. Related to the genus-one GT literature (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto), but the explicit factorization through GL_2(\hat Z) with det = χ is a modest point worth comparing.

missed.claim: Open program stated around this page: characterize Γ_Q inside Π~ (next page). Also determine what the splitting (3) of M~_{0,3} becomes in the genus-one extension Ñ_{1,1}.
missed.quote: il resterait encore à caractériser Γ_Q comme sous-groupe de Π~ (next page)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether GT equals Gal(Q̄/Q) is a well-known open question; here it appears in Grothendieck's own formulation. Not new as a problem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but largely expected step: extending a GT-type action from genus 0 to M_{1,1} via the ±1 extension and mapping to GL_2(\hat Z). The ideas overlap with later work (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Nakamura–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto, Ihara). Interesting as evidence that Grothendieck carried out the genus-one / GL_2 compatibility explicitly in unpublished notes, but no striking new result.
transcription_corrections: 'du § [?] (1)' is very likely 'du §39 (1)'; the next page refers to 'le diagramme (1) du §39'.
The geometric groups are written with a script C (Ĉ^+_{0,3}, Ĉ^+_{1,1}), not T̂, consistent with the next page's 'Ĉ^+_{0,3}'.
The middle groups are written with tildes: Ñ_{1,1} (N_{1,1}^~) and M~_{0,3}.
Under the arrow the target appears as 'Sl(2,Z)^' (Grothendieck's lowercase 'Sl'), with an equality/≅ sign.
The group symbol written 'Γ^~' looks like Π^~ in the handwriting (cf. next page 'Π^~'); 'Γ_{Q,σ}' is likewise possibly Π_{Q,σ}.
